title: A three-tier web application behind Amazon CloudFront
claim: Each request enters the VPC through the load balancer, and the instances and the database stay in private subnets.
alt: Users send requests to Amazon CloudFront. Amazon CloudFront forwards each request to an Application Load Balancer in the public subnets of a VPC. The load balancer forwards the request to one of two EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group in private subnets. The instances use a primary DB instance in other private subnets. The primary DB instance replicates to a standby DB instance in a Multi-AZ deployment.
notes: Pilot diagram. QA on 2026-10-04: 2 rounds, lint clean. No ports or limits are drawn, because the fact canon is still empty. Known limits: tiers are rows and no Availability Zone box is drawn, because groups cannot cross; the arrows from the load balancer enter the instances from the side, because a top entry runs through the group labels; the highlight ring on the load balancer was removed in round 2, because arrowheads overlap the ring.

edges.label: HTTPS
edges.say: A user sends an HTTPS request to Amazon CloudFront.
Amazon CloudFront forwards the request to its origin, the Application Load Balancer.
The load balancer forwards the request to a healthy instance in the Auto Scaling group.

edges.label: SQL
edges.say: The instance reads and writes data on the primary DB instance.

edges.label: replication
edges.say: Amazon RDS copies the data to the standby DB instance of the Multi-AZ deployment.
